title: Battle of Midway
subtitle: Central Pacific · 25 May – 7 June 1942
footnote: Midway local time (UTC−12); Japanese records run 21 hours ahead. Sinking positions from Nagumo's report, combinedfleet.com TROMs and the CINCPAC report; carrier positions at the moments of attack from the Enterprise and Yorktown action reports. Japanese approach tracks, the transport convoy and the Aleutian forces are reconstructed from bearings and distances. Formation members are spread slightly so they don't overlap.

kdb: Kido Butai weighs anchor at Hashirajima (06:00 JST 27 May): four carriers, two battleships, three cruisers, eleven destroyers
Fog — Nagumo breaks radio silence to order a course change
Only position fixed in Nagumo's report before the battle: 37°01.5′N 171°07′E, course 130°
Tomonaga's strike — 36 Kates, 36 Vals, 36 Zeros — launched about 240 nm north-west of Midway
PBY reports 'two carriers and battleships, bearing 320°, distance 180' — course 135°, 25 knots
Under attack by Midway's B-26s and Avengers; Tone's floatplane reports 'ten ships' to the north-east
Midway strike recovered; Nagumo turns to 070° to close the American carriers
Enterprise SBDs hit Kaga and Akagi, Yorktown's hit Sōryū — position from the Enterprise action report
Hiryū steams north launching her strikes; Nagumo's flag now in Nagara
Lt Samuel Adams (VS-5) sights Hiryū and her screen: 31°15′N 179°05′W
Hiryū hit by four 1,000-lb bombs — Enterprise action report position
Nagumo retires north-west at 18 knots; Yamamoto's order to pursue the enemy is ignored
Homeward bound; Nagara reaches Kure 13 June
hiryu: Kido Butai weighs anchor at Hashirajima (06:00 JST 27 May): four carriers, two battleships, three cruisers, eleven destroyers
Fog — Nagumo breaks radio silence to order a course change
Only position fixed in Nagumo's report before the battle: 37°01.5′N 171°07′E, course 130°
Tomonaga's strike — 36 Kates, 36 Vals, 36 Zeros — launched about 240 nm north-west of Midway
PBY reports 'two carriers and battleships, bearing 320°, distance 180' — course 135°, 25 knots
Under attack by Midway's B-26s and Avengers; Tone's floatplane reports 'ten ships' to the north-east
Midway strike recovered; Nagumo turns to 070° to close the American carriers
Enterprise SBDs hit Kaga and Akagi, Yorktown's hit Sōryū — position from the Enterprise action report
Hiryū steams north launching her strikes; Nagumo's flag now in Nagara
Lt Samuel Adams (VS-5) sights Hiryū and her screen: 31°15′N 179°05′W
Four 1,000-lb hits from Enterprise SBDs; fires out of control
main: Main Body sorties (06:00 JST 29 May): Yamato, Nagato, Mutsu, Hōshō, nine destroyers
About 300 nm behind Nagumo when the carriers are hit; Yamamoto learns of the disaster by radio
Yamamoto orders all forces to close and destroy the enemy in a night action
02:55 — 'Occupation of Midway is cancelled'; the fleet turns for home
Rendezvous with Nagumo's remnants; Kusaka and Genda are transferred to Yamato
kondo: Second Fleet sorties with the Main Body: Atago, Chōkai, Myōkō, Haguro, Kongō, Hiei, Zuihō, Yura
Swings south to shepherd the Midway invasion force
Ordered north-east at 28 knots to join Nagumo (grid YU MI KU 00 in Nagumo's report)
Racing to bring on a night surface action when Yamamoto cancels the operation
Retiring west; Kumano and Suzuya rejoin
crudiv7: Close Support Group sails from Guam (28 May JST): Kumano, Suzuya, Mikuma, Mogami, Arashio, Asashio
Covering the transport convoy from the north
Ordered to bombard Midway from 410 nm — Kurita works up to 35 knots
Bombardment cancelled; the division turns back
Surfaced USS Tambor sighted; in the emergency turn Mogami rams Mikuma — 90 nm west of Midway
Mogami (12 knots) and Mikuma trail oil; attacked by VMSB-241 and B-17s
Enterprise SBDs: five hits on Mikuma, two on Mogami
Mogami and Arashio leave the dying Mikuma with 240 survivors
Mogami limps toward Truk at 20 knots
transports: Twelve transports with 5,000 troops sail from Saipan (28 May JST), Jintsū and DesRon 2 escorting
Ens Jack Reid (VP-44): 'Main body' — eleven ships, 700 nm west of Midway
Nine B-17s attack from 8,000–12,000 ft; no hits
Four PBYs attack by moonlight; Akebono Maru torpedoed
Convoy reverses course on Yamamoto's orders
kakuta: Second Carrier Striking Force sails from Ōminato (26 May JST): Ryūjō, Jun'yō, Takao, Maya, three destroyers
Launches the Dutch Harbor strike from about 165 nm south-south-west
Second strike against destroyers in Makushin Bay aborted in icing cloud
Second-day strike launched from less than 100 nm south of Dutch Harbor
Ordered south to join Nagumo, then recalled
Covering the Kiska and Attu landings
hosogaya: Fifth Fleet main body sails: Nachi, two destroyers, oilers
Covers the invasion convoys from the south
kiska: Kiska Invasion Force sails (29 May JST): Kiso, Tama, Hibiki, Akatsuki, Hokaze, transports
Maizuru 3rd Special Naval Landing Force (about 500 men) lands on Kiska; the ten-man weather station is overrun
attu: Adak–Attu Invasion Force sails (29 May JST): Abukuma, four destroyers, transport Kinugasa Maru
Adak landing cancelled; diverted to Attu
Army North Sea Detachment (1,140 men) lands at Attu; 42 Aleuts and the two Americans at Chichagof Harbor taken
i168: Circles Midway submerged, reporting the defences
Shells Midway: six 100-mm rounds, driven down by searchlights and the coast guns
Sights the crippled Yorktown at 12 nm
Four torpedoes from 1,200 yd: two hit Yorktown, one Hammann
Surfaces after three hours and some 60 depth charges — and escapes
tf16: TF 16 sails: Enterprise, Hornet, six cruisers, nine destroyers — Spruance in Halsey's place
Point Luck — 32°N 173°W, 325 nm north-east of Midway, beyond Japanese search range
TF 17 joins; Fletcher takes tactical command
Dawn rendezvous point ordered by Fletcher: 31°30′N 176°30′W
Launch begins: 116 aircraft; the enemy estimated 155 nm away, bearing 239°
Recovering McClusky's survivors — and Yorktown's orphaned VB-3
Spruance retires east overnight rather than risk a night action against battleships
06:00 fix: 29°50′N 175°44′W, about 130 nm north-east of Midway
Launches 58 SBDs on a 300-mile search to the north-west
Hornet launches the first strike on the cruisers, 142 nm to the south-west
Hornet's second strike leaves; Mogami 110 nm to the west
Last aircraft recovered; TF 16 turns north-east to refuel
tf17: TF 17 sails: Yorktown, patched up in 48 hours, with Astoria, Portland and five destroyers
Joins TF 16 350 nm north-east of Midway
Launches ten SBDs to search the northern semicircle
Yorktown launches 17 SBDs, 12 TBDs and 6 F4Fs
Three bombs from Hiryū's Vals; Yorktown dead in the water by 12:40
Two torpedoes from Hiryū's Kates; Fletcher has already shifted to Astoria
Yorktown abandoned; Hughes stands by the hulk
Astoria and Portland join Spruance overnight
vireo: Fleet tug Vireo at Pearl and Hermes Reef
Takes Yorktown in tow at barely 2 knots
Cuts the tow as I-168's torpedoes strike; picks up survivors
nautilus: Patrolling on the 150-nm arc north-west of Midway
Sights smoke bearing 331°; under Zero strafing and Arashi's depth charges
Fires at Kirishima — one misfire, one miss
Four torpedoes at the burning Kaga from under 3,000 yd; one dud hit
tambor: Patrol station on the 150-nm circle west of Midway
'Many unidentified ships' at 3 nm — Cruiser Division 7 at 28 knots
Identifies two Mogami-class cruisers heading west, trailing oil
tf8: Theobald's TF 8 — Nashville, Indianapolis, Louisville, Honolulu, St Louis, four destroyers
Waits 400 nm south of Kodiak for an attack on the mainland that never comes

ships.name: Akagi
extra: One 1,000-lb bomb from Lt Richard Best detonates among fuelled and armed aircraft
Dead in the water, burning end to end; Capt Aoki orders abandon ship
Scuttled by four destroyer torpedoes on Yamamoto's order — 30°30′N 178°40′W
ships.sunkBy: Bomb hit by USS Enterprise SBD, scuttled by destroyers

ships.name: Kaga
extra: At least four 500- and 1,000-lb bombs; Capt Okada killed on the bridge
A dud torpedo from Nautilus breaks in half against her side
Two internal explosions and she sinks — 30°20′N 179°17′W

ships.name: Sōryū
extra: Three 1,000-lb bombs from Leslie's VB-3 in three minutes; abandoned by 10:45
Sinks after Isokaze's torpedoes; Capt Yanagimoto refuses to leave
ships.sunkBy: USS Yorktown SBDs (Leslie), scuttled by Isokaze

ships.name: Hiryū
extra: Abandon ship; Yamaguchi and Capt Kaku stay aboard
Sinks; 39 engineers still aboard escape in a boat and are found by USS Ballard 14 days later
ships.sunkBy: USS Enterprise SBDs, scuttled by Makigumo

ships.name: Arashi
ships.type: Destroyer — her wake led McClusky to the carriers

ships.name: Tanikaze
extra: Sent back to find Hiryū; 58 SBDs and B-17s attack — every bomb misses

ships.name: Kumano
extra: Kumano and Suzuya run on at full speed to join Kondō

ships.name: Mogami
ships.type: Heavy cruiser — bow crushed in the collision
damage: Turret hit; catapult deck bomb at 15:00

ships.name: Mikuma
extra: Her own torpedoes explode; the ship is gutted
Capsizes to port — 29°28′N 173°11′E, photographed by Enterprise SBDs at 17:15

ships.name: USS Yorktown
extra: Vireo takes the listing hulk in tow
Two torpedoes from I-168 open the starboard side

ships.name: USS Hammann
extra: Alongside Yorktown's starboard quarter with the salvage party's pumps and power
Broken in two by I-168's torpedo; her depth charges explode among the men in the water

ships.name: USS Hughes
extra: Guards the abandoned Yorktown overnight; picks up two men left aboard

strikes.name: Tomonaga strike on Midway
strikes.note: 36 Kates, 36 Vals and 36 Zeros wreck Sand and Eastern Islands' installations but leave the runways usable; VMF-221's Buffaloes are massacred. Tomonaga: 'There is need for a second attack'

strikes.name: Tone No. 4 search plane
strikes.note: Launched half an hour late by a catapult fault, PO Amari's Jake sights 'ten ships' at 07:28 — and at 08:20 adds 'accompanied by what appears to be a carrier'

strikes.name: Kobayashi dive-bomber strike (Hiryū)
strikes.note: 18 Vals and 6 Zeros; seven bombers break through Thach's Wildcats — three hits stop Yorktown. Five aircraft return

strikes.name: Tomonaga torpedo strike (Hiryū)
strikes.note: 10 Kates and 6 Zeros; Tomonaga presses in on one tank of fuel — two torpedo hits port side. Tomonaga does not return

strikes.name: Hōshō's search plane finds Hiryū
strikes.note: A Hōshō biplane photographs the abandoned Hiryū still afloat with men waving from her deck; Tanikaze is sent back to find her

strikes.name: Dutch Harbor strike (Ryūjō, Jun'yō)
strikes.note: Kates and Zeros from Ryūjō hit Fort Mears barracks (25 soldiers killed); most of Jun'yō's Vals turn back in the murk. A PBY is shot down

strikes.name: Dutch Harbor second-day strike
strikes.note: Fuel tanks, the hospital wing and SS Northwestern set ablaze. PO Koga's damaged Zero crash-lands on Akutan — the 'Akutan Zero'

strikes.name: PBY dawn search — Reid finds the convoy
strikes.note: Ens Jack Reid (VP-44): 'Main body, bearing 262, distance 700' — in fact Tanaka's transports. Nimitz corrects him: the carriers will come from the north-west

strikes.name: B-17s attack the convoy
strikes.note: Lt Col Walter Sweeney's Fortresses bomb from 8,000–12,000 ft, 570 nm out; no hits, but 'two battleships' claimed

strikes.name: PBY night torpedo attack
strikes.note: Lt William Richards' radar-equipped Catalinas find the convoy by moonlight; one torpedo hits the oiler Akebono Maru — the only American aerial torpedo hit of the battle

strikes.name: PBY search — Ady sights the carriers
strikes.note: Lt Howard Ady (VP-23) at 05:34: 'Two carriers and battleships bearing 320, distance 180, course 135, speed 25'

strikes.name: B-26s and VT-8 Avengers
strikes.note: Four Army Marauders and six Avengers of VT-8's Midway detachment attack with torpedoes: no hits, seven lost. One B-26 nearly crashes into Akagi's bridge

strikes.name: VMSB-241 — Henderson's Dauntlesses
strikes.note: Maj Lofton Henderson glide-bombs Hiryū with pilots who have barely flown the SBD; Henderson and seven others shot down, no hits

strikes.name: B-17s over the Kido Butai
strikes.note: Diverted from the convoy, Sweeney's Fortresses bomb from 20,000 ft — no hits

strikes.name: VMSB-241 — Norris's Vindicators
strikes.note: Maj Benjamin Norris's obsolete SB2Us glide-bomb Haruna; near-misses only, two lost

strikes.name: B-17 evening attacks
strikes.note: Twelve Fortresses in three groups bomb the burning Hiryū and her escorts and strafe the destroyer Tanikaze — no hits

strikes.name: VMSB-241 attacks the cruisers
strikes.note: Six SBDs and six SB2Us follow the oil slick to Mogami and Mikuma: near-misses. Capt Richard Fleming's burning Vindicator crashes into the sea beside Mikuma — Medal of Honor

strikes.name: B-17s attack the cruisers
strikes.note: Eight Fortresses; no hits

strikes.name: VT-8 — Waldron's Devastators
strikes.note: Lt Cdr John Waldron breaks from the Hornet group and finds the enemy alone. All fifteen TBDs are shot down; Ens George Gay, the only survivor, watches the battle from the water

strikes.name: VT-6 — Lindsey's Devastators
strikes.note: Lt Cdr Eugene Lindsey attacks Kaga without fighter cover: ten of fourteen lost, Lindsey among them, no hits

strikes.name: Hornet air group — the 'flight to nowhere'
strikes.note: Cdr Stanhope Ring leads 35 SBDs and 10 F4Fs west along a course that misses the Japanese. All ten Wildcats run out of fuel and ditch; VS-8 lands at Midway

strikes.name: McClusky — Enterprise dive bombers
strikes.note: Finding empty sea, Lt Cdr Wade McClusky follows the destroyer Arashi's wake north. VS-6 and VB-6 put four bombs into Kaga; Lt Richard Best's section peels off and hits Akagi once — enough

strikes.name: Leslie's VB-3 with VT-3 and Thach's VF-3
strikes.note: Lt Cdr Lance Massey's VT-3 draws the Zeros down to sea level (ten of twelve lost); above them Lt Cdr Max Leslie's 17 SBDs hit Sōryū three times in three minutes. Thach's four F4Fs invent the 'Thach weave' on the way in

strikes.name: Yorktown's afternoon search finds Hiryū
strikes.note: Ten VS-5 Dauntlesses; Lt Samuel Adams reports one carrier, two battleships, three cruisers and four destroyers at 31°15′N 179°05′W

strikes.name: Enterprise strike on Hiryū
strikes.note: 24 SBDs (fourteen of them Yorktown orphans) — four 1,000-lb hits blow Hiryū's forward flight deck onto the bridge. The last Japanese carrier is finished

strikes.name: Hornet strike on the screen
strikes.note: Arriving after Hiryū is ablaze, Hornet's 16 SBDs go for Haruna and Tone — near-misses only

strikes.name: TF 16 search-strike — Tanikaze
strikes.note: 58 Dauntlesses fly 300 miles north-west hunting a 'burning carrier' and find only the destroyer Tanikaze, which dodges every bomb; one SBD lost. The first night carrier landings for most pilots

strikes.name: Enterprise dawn search
strikes.note: Eighteen SBDs; the crippled Mikuma and Mogami reported as a 'battleship and carrier' at 29°33′N 174°30′E

strikes.name: Hornet strike 1 on the cruisers
strikes.note: 26 SBDs and 8 F4Fs; Mogami's No. 5 turret hit (18 killed), Mikuma and the destroyers strafed. One SBD lost

strikes.name: Enterprise strike on the cruisers
strikes.note: 31 SBDs, 3 TBDs and 12 F4Fs: five 1,000-lb hits on Mikuma, two on Mogami; at 13:58 Mikuma's torpedoes explode

strikes.name: Hornet strike 2 on the cruisers
strikes.note: Another hit on Mikuma and a 1,000-lb bomb through Mogami's catapult deck into her sick bay; Arashio hit — 37 Mikuma survivors on her deck killed. Enterprise SBDs return at 17:15 to photograph the wreck

torpedoes.note: One hit in the bow; 11 killed, the oiler keeps station
One tube misfires, the other torpedo misses; Arashi is left behind to hold Nautilus down
One hits and breaks in two without exploding — Kaga's swimmers cling to the floating air flask
Two hits port side; rudder jammed, list 26° within minutes
Scuttling; Kaga sinks after two internal explosions
Yamamoto's 'Dispose of Akagi' — Nowaki, Arashi, Hagikaze and Maikaze fire one torpedo each
One hit; Hiryū stays afloat another four hours
Fired in two pairs from 1,200 yd under the escorts' sonar screen: two hit Yorktown, one Hammann, one runs astern
Hammann's back is broken; she sinks in four minutes

engagements.note: Anti-aircraft fire against six successive attacks from Midway and the carriers
Hiryū's screen against the Enterprise and Hornet strikes and the B-17s
Against Tomonaga's Kates; Balch and Benham detached from TF 16
Six 100-mm rounds toward Sand Island; the Marines' 7-inch battery replies
Three carrier strikes in five hours

events: Kakuta's Second Carrier Striking Force sails from Ōminato for the Aleutians
Kido Butai sails from Hashirajima
Station HYPO's decrypts convince Nimitz that 'AF' is Midway and the attack will come 4 June
TF 16 sails from Pearl Harbor under Spruance
Yamamoto's Main Body and Kondō's Second Fleet sortie from Hashirajima
Yorktown, repaired in 48 hours, sails with TF 17
Operation K: the Japanese flying-boat reconnaissance of Pearl Harbor is abandoned — US ships are sitting on the French Frigate Shoals refuelling point
TF 16 and TF 17 meet at Point Luck, 325 nm north-east of Midway
Nagumo, in fog, fixes his position at 37°01′N 171°07′E and turns onto 130° for Midway
Dutch Harbor bombed: Fort Mears barracks hit, 25 soldiers killed
PBY sights the invasion convoy 700 nm west of Midway — 'Main body'
Nine B-17s bomb the convoy — no hits
PBYs torpedo the oiler Akebono Maru by moonlight
Nagumo launches 108 aircraft against Midway
'Two carriers and battleships' — PBY sights the Kido Butai
VMF-221's 25 fighters meet the Japanese strike 30 nm out; 15 are shot down
Midway bombed: power plant, hangars, fuel tanks — but the runways survive
Midway-based B-26s and TBFs open the attack on the carriers
Nagumo orders his reserve Kates rearmed with land bombs
Tone's No. 4 plane: 'accompanied by what appears to be a carrier' — Nagumo dithers
VT-8 annihilated: fifteen Devastators, one survivor
Kaga hit
Sōryū hit
Akagi hit — three carriers ablaze in six minutes
Nagumo hoists his flag in Nagara
Yorktown takes three bombs from Hiryū's dive bombers
Fletcher shifts his flag to Astoria
Nautilus torpedoes the burning Kaga — a dud
Yorktown scout sights Hiryū
Yorktown torpedoed twice; abandoned at 15:00
Hiryū hit by four bombs
Sōryū sinks
Kaga sinks
Nagumo retires north-west
I-168 shells Midway
Mogami rams Mikuma while evading USS Tambor
Yamamoto cancels the Midway operation
Akagi scuttled
Marine bombers attack the damaged cruisers; Capt Fleming killed
Hiryū sinks with Yamaguchi and Kaku aboard
Vireo takes Yorktown in tow
58 Dauntlesses bomb the destroyer Tanikaze — and miss
Japanese troops land on Kiska
Enterprise scouts find Mikuma and Mogami
I-168 torpedoes Yorktown and Hammann
Hammann sinks — 80 killed
Mikuma's torpedoes explode
Mikuma sinks
Japanese troops land on Attu
Yorktown sinks
Maj Gen Clarence Tinker, commanding 7th Air Force, lost leading a B-24 raid on Wake

ports.name: Hashirajima
ports.note: Combined Fleet anchorage in the Inland Sea; Kido Butai and Main Body sortie from here

ports.name: Kure
ports.note: Naval arsenal; Nagara lands Kido Butai's 618 wounded and survivors here on 14 June

ports.name: Ōminato
ports.note: Northern Force base at the head of Mutsu Bay

ports.name: Paramushiro
ports.note: Kuriles staging anchorage for the Kiska and Attu invasion forces

ports.name: Saipan
ports.note: Transport Group with 5,000 troops of the Ichiki Detachment and Kure 5th SNLF sails 28 May

ports.name: Guam
ports.note: Kurita's Close Support Group (CruDiv 7) sails 28 May

ports.name: Wake
ports.note: Japanese since 23 Dec 1941; land-based air support for the invasion

ports.name: Truk
ports.note: Mogami limps here for repair after the battle

ports.name: Midway — NAS Midway / MAG-22
ports.note: Sand and Eastern Islands: 32 PBYs, 17 B-17s, 4 B-26s, 6 TBFs, VMF-221 (28 fighters), VMSB-241 (34 bombers); 6th Defense Battalion, 3,652 men

ports.name: Kure Atoll
ports.note: Uninhabited atoll 55 nm west of Midway; reconnoitred by I-168 on 31 May

ports.name: Pearl and Hermes Reef
ports.note: Vireo's station; the tug sails from here to tow Yorktown

ports.name: French Frigate Shoals
ports.note: Seaplane tenders Thornton and Ballard occupy the lagoon — denying the Japanese flying boats their refuelling point for Operation K

ports.name: Pearl Harbor
ports.note: Pacific Fleet base; Yorktown repaired here in 48 hours

ports.name: Dutch Harbor
ports.note: Naval Operating Base and Fort Mears, Unalaska; bombed 3 and 4 June — 43 killed, 14 aircraft, SS Northwestern burnt out

ports.name: Kodiak
ports.note: Theobald's North Pacific Force base; PatWing 4 Catalinas

ports.name: Kiska
ports.note: Ten-man Navy weather station; occupied by the Japanese 6 June (2 killed, 7 captured)

ports.name: Attu
ports.note: Aleut village at Chichagof Harbor; occupied by the Japanese 7 June

ports.name: Pearl Harbor — CINCPAC / Station HYPO
ports.note: Nimitz's headquarters and Cdr Joseph Rochefort's Combat Intelligence Unit, whose JN-25 decrypts gave the date, place and order of battle of the attack

rescues.note: Hagikaze and Maikaze lift some 900 of Kaga's 1,700-man crew from the water
Isokaze and Hamakaze take off Sōryū's survivors; 711 are lost
Arashi, Nowaki, Hagikaze and Maikaze embark Akagi's crew through the night before scuttling her
Makigumo and Kazagumo take off about 800 men; 39 engineers trapped below escape after she has been left
Hammann, Balch, Benham, Russell and Anderson take 2,270 men off the listing carrier
Mogami and Arashio embark 240 survivors and leave; Trout picks up two more on 9 June
Benham takes 171 of Hammann's 251; Vireo and Hughes recover the salvage party

kdb.name: Vice Admiral Chūichi Nagumo
kdb.bio: The victor of Pearl Harbor and the Indian Ocean raid, a torpedo and destroyer specialist commanding carriers he did not fully understand. Caught between rearming for a second strike on Midway and the sudden report of an American carrier, he chose to recover his aircraft and launch a co-ordinated blow — and was hit with his decks full of fuelled and armed planes.

hiryu.name: Rear Admiral Tamon Yamaguchi
hiryu.bio: Aggressive and widely tipped as a future Combined Fleet commander, he urged Nagumo at 08:30 to 'launch attack force immediately' with what was on deck. Left with the only surviving carrier, he struck Yorktown twice and was preparing a dusk attack when Hiryū was hit.
hiryu.fate: Chose to go down with Hiryū with her captain, Tomeo Kaku, 5 June 1942.

main.name: Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto
main.bio: Architect of Pearl Harbor and of Operation MI, which he meant to force the decisive battle before American production told. He kept his battleships 300 miles behind the carriers and radio silence kept him ignorant of the intelligence Nagumo lacked. Ordered a night pursuit, then at 02:55 cancelled the operation.
main.fate: Shot down over Bougainville by P-38s, 18 April 1943.

kondo.name: Vice Admiral Nobutake Kondō
kondo.bio: Commanded the invasion force's covering group of two battleships and four heavy cruisers. Raced north-east at 28 knots to bring on a night action that Spruance's withdrawal east denied him.

crudiv7.name: Vice Admiral Takeo Kurita
crudiv7.bio: Ordered at 13:50 on 4 June to bombard Midway with four heavy cruisers, then recalled 90 miles short; a surfaced American submarine caused the turn in which Mogami rammed Mikuma. Two and a half years later he would command Center Force at Leyte Gulf.

transports.name: Rear Admiral Raizō Tanaka
transports.role: Commander, Destroyer Squadron 2 — Transport Group escort
transports.bio: Escorted the twelve transports carrying 5,000 troops from Saipan. His convoy was the first Japanese force sighted, on 3 June, and the only one attacked that night. Later the master of the Guadalcanal 'Tokyo Express'.

kakuta.name: Rear Admiral Kakuji Kakuta
kakuta.bio: Struck Dutch Harbor on two days with the light carrier Ryūjō and the converted liner Jun'yō. His force was briefly ordered south to reinforce Nagumo and then recalled to cover the Kiska and Attu landings.
kakuta.fate: Presumed to have killed himself on Tinian, August 1944.

hosogaya.name: Vice Admiral Boshirō Hosogaya
hosogaya.bio: In overall command of Operation AL — the Aleutians diversion and the occupation of Kiska and Attu, the only objectives of the whole plan that were achieved.
hosogaya.fate: Relieved after the Komandorski Islands, March 1943; died 1964.

i168.name: Lt Cdr Yahachi Tanabe
i168.bio: Reconnoitred Kure Atoll and Midway, shelled the atoll on the night of 4/5 June, then found the abandoned Yorktown by a Chikuma floatplane's report and crept under her destroyer screen to fire four torpedoes from 1,200 yards — the Japanese Navy's only consolation of the battle.

tf16.name: Rear Admiral Raymond A. Spruance
tf16.bio: A cruiser admiral with no aviation background, given Halsey's carriers when Halsey went into hospital with shingles. Accepted his chief of staff Miles Browning's advice to launch at extreme range at 07:00, and — as decisively — turned east on the night of 4 June rather than blunder into Yamamoto's battleships.

tf17.name: Rear Admiral Frank Jack Fletcher
tf17.role: Commander, Task Force 17 — officer in tactical command
tf17.bio: Commanded at Coral Sea a month earlier and brought the damaged Yorktown back into the fight after 48 hours in dry dock. Held Yorktown's strike back until the enemy was fixed, launched Leslie's decisive group, and with his flagship crippled handed tactical command to Spruance that evening: 'Will conform to your movements.'

nautilus.name: Lt Cdr William H. Brockman
nautilus.bio: Pushed his big old submarine into the middle of the Kido Butai on the morning of 4 June. The destroyer Arashi, left behind to depth-charge him, was the ship whose wake McClusky followed to the carriers.

tf8.name: Rear Admiral Robert A. Theobald
tf8.bio: Given the Aleutians and told by Nimitz's intelligence that Dutch Harbor and Kiska were the targets, he disbelieved it and kept his cruisers 400 miles south of Kodiak to guard against a landing on the mainland. His force never saw the Japanese.
